edits.old_text: The study is delimited to the development and evaluation of a functional software prototype intended for a single-clinic teleconsultation environment. Enterprise-level cloud scaling, multi-hospital deployment, and integration with external Electronic Health Records (EHR) and Hospital Information Systems (HIS) are excluded from the scope of the study.
edits.replacement: The prototype targets one doctor and one patient per encounter at a single dental clinic. Its maximum safe number of simultaneous encounters was not measured. Provider quotas are not validated application capacity. Multi-clinic operation, enterprise scaling, and external EHR/HIS integration remain outside the study.
edits.reason: State an intended encounter size without inventing a concurrent-call result.

edits.old_text: The modular architecture and cloud-based services provide a foundation for possible future improvements, including additional users, expanded clinical workflows, and integration with other healthcare information systems. However, large-scale scalability, performance under high concurrent demand, and multi-clinic deployment were not independently evaluated
edits.replacement: The cloud services provide a foundation for future expansion, not a measured capacity guarantee. At the 25 November 2026 documentation check, LiveKit Build listed 100 concurrent connections, 5,000 participant-minutes and 50 GB downstream transfer per month (livekit.com/pricing). These are service allowances, not proof of 50 safe consultations. High-load performance and multi-clinic deployment were not independently evaluated
edits.reason: Distinguish documented allowance from measured system capacity; preserve the continuation on the next page.

edits.old_text: The platform also interacts with several external services to support its operations. Firebase Authentication handles user authentication, while Google Identity Provider supports Google-based sign-in through Firebase Authentication. LiveKit Cloud facilitates real-time consultation communication and participant media exchange. The OpenAI API processes consultation context to generate AI-assisted consultation summaries, while the ip-api.com Geolocation API provides coarse geolocation information during invitation validation.
edits.replacement: Firebase Authentication and Google Identity Provider support account sign-in. LiveKit Cloud transports real-time media, while the OpenAI API supports optional, evidence-grounded summary generation. The figures are logical component maps: legacy geolocation and attachment paths do not represent enabled production features. Current admission does not use ip-api.com, device fingerprints, or location as proof of identity.
edits.reason: Remove claims that removed geolocation is an active access control.

edits.old_text: The first process, Manage Access and Admission, handles user authentication, account access, invitation validation, and waiting-room admission. It facilitates interactions with patients and dentists while utilizing Firebase Authentication and Google Identity Provider for authentication and the Geolocation API for location-related information during invitation validation. User profiles and role information, as well as invitation and waiting-room records, are maintained through the corresponding logical data stores.
edits.replacement: The first process, Manage Access and Admission, verifies Firebase identities and persisted invitation policy on the server. Only a provider-verified, allowlisted account may bypass waiting; other visitors require clinician admission. Invitation possession, typed email, location, and device information are not identity proof. User profiles, invitations, and waiting records occupy separate logical stores.
edits.reason: Align the diagram explanation with actual verified-account admission policy.

edits.old_text: The third process, Manage Consultation Records and Summaries, handles clinical documentation, consultation history, uploaded clinical files, and AI-assisted summary generation. It processes clinical notes and consultation transcripts, retrieves relevant consultation information, and interacts with the OpenAI API to generate consultation summaries when the service is available and enabled. The resulting documentation and summaries are stored for subsequent retrieval by authorized patients and dentists.
edits.replacement: The third process manages session-bound records and optional AI summaries. Authorized patients receive their visit history; clinicians receive authorized clinical summaries. Generation requires usable consented transcript evidence and service availability; drafts require clinician review. File attachments are prepared but disabled, and chat text is not currently a clinical summary input.
edits.reason: Separate patient history, clinician-only summary content, disabled files, and actual prompt evidence.

edits.old_text: The fourth process, Perform Audit and Retention Operations, supports backend operational activities, particularly automated audit logging and consultation summary retention. It receives relevant record changes from the application's data repositories, generates audit and activity records, and performs scheduled deletion of consultation summaries according to the implemented retention policy.
edits.replacement: The fourth process supports audits and opt-in summary retention. Firebase's daily deletion worker defaults to a 30-day cutoff; Vercel's separate cron retries summary processing. Neither age nor a missing summary proves deletion. Sessions, transcripts, messages, other copies and backups are not fully purged. Future attachments need a separate approved expiry policy, bounded storage/metadata cleanup, and retry reconciliation; uploads remain disabled.
edits.reason: Do not promise enabled or complete 30-day deletion.

edits.old_text: The diagram incorporates seven logical data stores representing user profiles and roles, invitation and waiting-room records, room and session records, chat messages, clinical documentation and summaries, uploaded clinical files, and audit and activity records. These logical stores are implemented using Firebase Firestore and Firebase Storage, which serve as the platform's underlying persistence technologies.
edits.replacement: The seven logical stores describe profiles, access, sessions, chat, clinical records, prepared attachments, and audits. Firestore implements structured persistence. Firebase Storage is a prepared binary-storage dependency, not an enabled clinical upload service. Logical relationships require application controls; the diagrams do not establish database-enforced foreign keys or cascades.
edits.reason: Avoid treating prepared storage paths as operational uploads or SQL constraints.

edits.old_text: In addition to internal tier-to-tier communications, the architecture integrates specialized external cloud services through dedicated bidirectional interfaces: Firebase Authentication interfaces with the Google Identity Provider for secure Google Sign-in; the Presentation and Application layers connect directly with LiveKit Cloud for WebRTC real- time media transport and communication; the Application layer communicates with the OpenAI API for automated AI summary processing; and backend services dispatch calls to ip-api.com for client geolocation and IP lookup requests. This modular stratification ensures high security, scalability, and maintainability across all operational levels of the platform.
edits.replacement: Firebase Authentication integrates Google sign-in. Browser clients exchange media with LiveKit Cloud; application routes issue scoped credentials and process verified webhooks. Optional OpenAI processing receives authorized session evidence, not the full database. Geolocation lookup is not an active admission dependency. This layered design separates control, media, and persistence responsibilities; it does not independently prove clinical fitness, regulatory compliance, capacity, or guaranteed latency.
edits.reason: Replace obsolete geolocation and unconditional security/scalability assurance.

edits.old_text: During the consultation, the platform facilitates video and audio communication, real-time messaging, screen sharing, and the management of consultation-related information. Upon completion of the session, the system processes clinical documentation and generates AI-assisted consultation summaries, which are stored for authorized access and future reference. Additionally, background operations support activity logging and the retention management of consultation records.
edits.replacement: During consultation, audio, video, chat and screen sharing are available. An invitation is reusable access policy; each room opening may create a distinct encounter. Active encounters are not finalized and cannot generate a summary. Leaving or lifecycle events may finalize an encounter without revoking its invitation. Finalized processing still requires consent, usable evidence, availability and revision guards; reviewed output is preserved. Doctor-only openings are nonclinical records, not diagnoses.
edits.reason: Clarify triggers versus eligibility and provider invocation.

edits.old_text: Once the dentist admits the patient, both actors establish a secure media handshake to Patient and Dentist join LiveKit room, transitioning into active consultation workflows featuring multi-modal video, audio, screen sharing, and real-time text chat. Following the session, the clinician records clinical notes and file attachments before triggering the automated termination sequence. At this stage, the backend executes sequential processes to finalize the
edits.replacement: After server-authorized admission, the doctor and patient can join the LiveKit room and exchange audio, video, screen sharing, and chat. A verified allowlisted account may join directly. File uploads are disabled. Optional transcript capture requires consent. Patient departure or another authorized lifecycle event can request finalization; it is not limited to a clinician pressing Revoke. The backend then attempts to finalize the
edits.reason: Correct disabled files, direct admission, and lifecycle trigger description.

edits.old_text: maintains information about files uploaded and shared within those sessions. The CALL_SUMMARY entity stores consultation summaries and their associated information, including key points, recommendations, follow-up actions, and other relevant details. The relationships among these entities are represented through primary keys (PK) and foreign keys (FK), which identify records and establish logical associations between related data.

edits.old_text: 1. Client Devices / User Network Tier: Comprising the Patient and Doctor Web Browsers, this tier represents the entry point where end-users interact with the client- side Next.js user interfaces. Client devices communicate securely with the web application tier over encrypted HTTPS / TLS 1.3 channels for standard web navigation and API requests. Furthermore, clients interact directly with managed backend services using client-side SDKs, including Firebase Auth SDK for user authentication, Firebase client SDK for real-time Firestore queries and consultation records, and Firebase Storage SDK for direct binary file uploads.
edits.replacement: 1. Client Devices / User Network Tier: Patient and doctor browsers use HTTPS for the Next.js interface and API requests, Firebase Authentication for sign-in, and authorized Firestore client subscriptions for selected updates. Sensitive consultation operations use server-owned authorization. Browser media travels through LiveKit WebRTC, not through Firestore or the Vercel page server. Direct Firebase Storage uploads are disabled. HTTPS transport does not establish independently verified end-to-end media encryption.
edits.reason: Correct media topology and disabled direct uploads without claiming a fixed TLS version or E2EE.

edits.old_text: 3. Cloud Services / Firebase Backend Tier: Comprising managed backend-as-a-service (BaaS) infrastructure, this tier handles persistent storage and security enforcement. Firebase Authentication integrates with the Google Identity Provider to facilitate secure OAuth sign-in workflows. Cloud Firestore maintains structured NoSQL records for rooms, invitations, and session metadata, while Firebase Storage secures binary chat attachments and clinical documents. Additionally, Firebase Cloud Functions execute asynchronous backend logic driven by Firestore triggers, automatically managing audit logging and scheduled data retention policies.
edits.replacement: 3. Cloud Services / Firebase Backend Tier: Firebase Authentication handles accounts; Firestore stores structured access and encounter records. Cloud Functions support audit triggers and opt-in summary retention. Firebase Storage is prepared for binary files, but clinical uploads are disabled. The database holds text and metadata, not routine full-call video recordings. Retention must be approved and verified before routine clinical deployment.
edits.reason: Distinguish stored records from transported video and inactive storage.

edits.old_text: The researchers configured the TeleConsole application and its integrated cloud services to support the platform's primary functions. Firebase Authentication and Google Identity Provider were configured to support user authentication, while Cloud Firestore was used to manage application records, consultation information, and other relevant data. Firebase Storage was used for supported document and attachment storage. The OpenAI API was integrated to support AI-assisted consultation summary generation, while the ip-api.com Geolocation API provided location- related information during invitation validation. edits.replacement: Firebase Authentication and Google sign-in support accounts; Firestore stores application and encounter records. LiveKit Cloud handles audio, video and screen sharing. Booking grants no admission or clinical evidence and was not surveyed. ip-api.com is not an admission dependency. JWT, webhook and ownership checks are layered controls, not certification. Clinic release still requires verified rules/indexes, retention, restore, provider agreements, recurring budget and measured call quality/concurrency.

edits.old_text: Concurrently, the Doctor actor initiates authentication via sign-in, creates and manages consultation rooms and invitations, manages the waiting queue by admitting or rejecting patients, conducts live audio and video consultations, utilizes real-time chat and screen sharing, controls hardware peripherals, adds consultation notes and attachments, views clinical history, reviews and edits summaries, and terminates or leaves the session. Furthermore, system-level execution patterns are governed by mandatory inclusion dependencies, where joining an admitted consultation requires validating access credentials, participating in live video sessions triggers media connection protocols, and ending a consultation automatically invokes the backend generation of an AI-assisted clinical summary.
edits.replacement: Staff use Firebase Authentication; signup grants no administrative role. Platform and clinic administrators manage staff access without clinician API permissions, even with old combined claims. Clinic administrators provision doctors in their clinic; legacy profiles remain transitional. A separate doctor account manages invitations, admission, calls and draft review. Verified allowlisted patients may enter directly. Admission is permission, not attendance; the host is not a patient visit. Attachments remain disabled. Doctor-booked appointments are implemented but deployment-gated, separate from admission and encounters. Summary processing requires finalization, consent and usable evidence. Administration does not confer clinical record ownership.
edits.reason: Align the actor description with verified direct entry, clinician admission, disabled attachments and conditional AI finalization.
